Folks — ran a tabletop against the wiring diagram and telcoco_rack_map_rev3.pdf. Notes below (technical):

1) Control-plane reachability
- Probes: I validated TCP/443 and our management port 9000 via a simulated NAT/PE hairpin. If your edge boxes terminate TCP with TLS inspection, we need a passthrough policy for the VIP CIDRs.
- Keepalive/Probing: our KV replication uses short-lived TLS sessions; if there is aggressive TCP connection timeout on the firewall (under 60s) we will see RTOs. Recommend configuring TCP idle to >= 300s for the VIP range.

2) Data-plane egress and BGP
- BGP communities: we'll tag sync traffic with community 65001:100 to ensure it egresses via the preferred BGP peer. Confirm acceptance of custom communities.
- Route propagation: TelcoCo should not de-aggregate the /24 we hand off; we rely on stable prefix advertisement for node-level affinity.

3) Management VLAN + bootstrap
- If the management VLAN is untagged on the patch panel, we can use DHCP with relay; otherwise we will require pre-provisioned DHCP on the management VLAN with an option 121 route to the bootstrap server.

4) KMS/HSM and key handling (Kimberly)
- Expecting a per-tenant key wrap key stored in your HSM. We will request an SKI and an OTP provisioning flow; will want a test key for the first rack.

Attachments referenced: controlplane-dataplane-wiring-v2.pdf (I annotated), telcoco-keystore-profiles.csv (key profile examples).

Next steps and timeline
- Friday EOD: TelcoCo to provide gap list for patch panel + BGP community acceptance.
- Monday AM: Jordan to run an in-situ TCP probe from Redwood edge (if cross-connect present) and share raw probe logs.

-jb
